method: Searched 2026-10-31 (UTC). Discovery: web search (the GitHub search API and github.com/search are blocked in this session; gist.github.com clones were refused by the proxy), then followed references in papers, READMEs, Concretum tutorials and QuantConnect forum threads. Each repo was checked with `git ls-remote`, shallow-cloned (`git clone --depth 1`, sparse checkout for the three large frameworks) into a new empty directory under scratchpad/research/repos/<owner>__<repo>, and its SHA recorded with `git rev-parse HEAD`. Code was only read (cat/grep/sed, and notebook JSON parsed as text); no install scripts, setup.py, notebooks or repo code were run. Papers were read from author/institutional PDFs (HSG Alexandria for the Zarattini et al. papers, a working-paper PDF for Gao et al.) or, when paywalled, at abstract level via IDEAS/RePEc, SSRN and university pages. All web pages and PDFs were read through a fetch tool that returns an extract or summary rather than the raw file, so long PDFs may have been truncated, and figures were cross-checked against a second source where one existed. The depth of reading is stated in each entry's evidence field. Author numbers are copied as reported and treated as claims; stars, equity curves and win rates were not used as evidence. entries.name: Beat the Market: noise-area intraday momentum on SPY (Zarattini, Aziz, Barbon 2024)
entries.source_version: SFI Research Paper 24-97 (May 2024), full PDF from HSG Alexandria; plus Concretum's Python/Alpaca tutorial code quoted on concretumgroup.com
entries.license: author copyright (working paper); tutorial code license not stated
entries.what: Trend-following on SPY: go with the move once price leaves a 'noise area' built from the average absolute move away from the open at the same time of day over the prior 14 days. Exits use a VWAP/band trailing stop, decisions are made only every 30 minutes, and the position is flat at the close.
entries.entry: At HH:00 and HH:30 only. sigma(t) = mean over the prior 14 sessions of |close(t)/open - 1| at that minute. UB = max(today open, prior close) x (1 + sigma); LB = min(today open, prior close) x (1 - sigma). Go long if the price is above UB, short if below LB (the tutorial also requires being on the same side of VWAP).
entries.exit: Trailing stop: max(UB, VWAP) for longs and min(LB, VWAP) for shorts, checked at the semi-hourly marks. Crossing the opposite boundary reverses the position. Flat at 16:00.
entries.sizing: Shares = prior-day equity x min(4, 2% target daily vol / SPY trailing daily vol) / open price; leverage capped at 4x.
entries.timeframe: 1-minute bars, decisions every 30 minutes, intraday only
entries.data: Paper: IQFeed 1m SPY and VIX, May 2007 to Apr 2024 (paid). Tutorial: Alpaca free-key SIP raw 1m bars, 2018-01-01 to 2024-06-05. Schwab 1m bars plus daily dividends are enough to replicate.
entries.reported: Net of costs: total return 1,985%, annualized 19.6%, volatility 14.3%, Sharpe 1.33, max drawdown 25%, hit ratio about 43%. Costs: commission $0.0035/share and slippage $0.001/share. Under the I-Star slippage model the Sharpe falls to 1.17. The 90-day lookback had the best Sharpe (1.50). The Alpaca tutorial, which adds an overnight-gap reversal leg and models no slippage, reports 2018 to Jun 2024: total 472%, annualized 31.3%, Sharpe 1.95, max drawdown 10%, hit rate 48%.
entries.evidence: Author-reported only. No independent replication was found on QuantConnect, CXO, GitHub or the web. The authors run Concretum Group and Bear Bull Traders, which sell research and education. The paper has internal inconsistencies: the worst day is -4.8% in the text and -4.5% in Table A1, and the Sharpe appears as both 1.33 and 1.35. The underlying effect (intraday time-series momentum on index products) is independently documented in Gao et al. (2018 JFE) and Baltussen et al. (2021 JFE). The robustness section covers VIX buckets, weekday, NR4/NR7 days, cost levels and lookback, but has no walk-forward or held-out period.
entries.risks: Concretum Python code as quoted: exposure is shift(1) and P&L = exposure x close.diff(), so entry happens at the close of the signal bar, with zero latency and no spread beyond commission. Stops are only evaluated at the semi-hourly marks, so losses between checks are not capped. sigma_open is correctly lagged (rolling 14 per minute-of-day, then shift(1)), so there is no look-ahead in the bands. The vol estimate uses daily returns iloc[d-15:d-1], which skips the latest day (conservative). The best lookback and band multiplier were found on the full sample. 4x leverage cannot be replicated one-to-one with options. VWAP is built from (H+L+C)/3 typical prices, not trades.
entries.reusable: Time-of-day-specific noise bands; VWAP trailing stop; semi-hourly decision grid as an anti-chop device; vol-target sizing; regime diagnostics (VIX/realized-vol buckets, NR4/NR7 days).
entries.fit: Very good. SPY and QQQ, 1m bars, one position and a few decisions a day. Options can be modeled as near-dated ATM calls/puts once live spreads are recorded going forward (we have no historical option quotes).
entries.rank_why: Provisional A. The rules and code are public and reproducible on our exact data, costs and slippage are modeled, and the mechanism is independently documented in peer-reviewed work. The performance numbers are still author-only, so our own replication decides.
entries.next: Replicate on Schwab 1m SPY and QQQ bars: (1) paper rules with fills at the next bar open plus a 1-cent spread and $0.001/share slippage; (2) paper defaults frozen (band multiplier 1, 14-day lookback), no tuning; (3) results by year and by our realized-vol tercile; (4) MAE between half-hour checks to size the gap risk of the coarse stop; (5) from today, record ATM 0-2 DTE option bid/ask at every signal time for an options cost overlay.

entries.name: Market Intraday Momentum (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou 2018)
entries.source_version: Journal of Financial Economics 129(2):394-414 (Aug 2018). I read the Dec 2015 working paper ('Intraday Momentum: The First Half-Hour Return Predicts the Last Half-Hour Return'). SSRN id is cited as 2440866 by one source and 2552752 by QuantRocket; I verified neither.
entries.license: publisher copyright (Elsevier); working paper publicly posted
entries.what: The first half-hour return of SPY, measured from the prior close to 10:00, predicts the last half-hour return. A timing strategy trades only the last 30 minutes in the direction of that signal.
entries.entry: At 15:30 ET, go long SPY if r1 = P(10:00)/prior 16:00 close - 1 > 0, otherwise short (eta(r1)). The variant eta(r1, r12) also uses the 15:00-15:30 return.
entries.exit: Market close (16:00).
entries.sizing: Unit exposure; no leverage or vol targeting in the paper's timing test.
entries.instruments: SPY; also QQQ, XLF, IWM, DIA, EEM, FXI, EFA, VWO, IYR, TLT and FTSE 100 / EuroStoxx 50 futures
entries.timeframe: Half-hour returns; one decision per day, held for the last 30 minutes
entries.data: TAQ SPY trades, Feb 1993 to Dec 2013 (paid). Replication needs only free 1m bars plus the official prior close.
entries.reported: Working paper: in-sample R^2 1.6% (r1), 1.1% (r12), 2.6% (both); out-of-sample R^2 1.2%, 0.7%, 1.8%. eta(r1): about 6.67%/yr average, 6.19% sd, Sharpe 1.08, 54.37% success, versus buy-and-hold 6.04%/yr and Sharpe 0.29. High-volatility days: 14.73%/yr (Sharpe 1.63). High-volume days: 11.87%/yr (Sharpe 1.38). Recessions: 16.79%/yr versus 2.35% in expansions (eta(r1,r12)). After bid-ask costs, post-July 2001 about 4.46%/yr; post-2005 about 6.52% versus 7.96% before costs. Commissions ignored.
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed, with out-of-sample tests by the authors. Li, Sakkas and Urquhart (2022, J. Financial Markets 57:100619; 16 developed markets, 1m data, Oct 2005 to Dec 2017): predictability in 12 of 16 markets in-sample, but unconstrained out-of-sample R^2 is positive in only 5 of 16. Baltussen et al. (2021) find the effect in 60+ futures, 1974 to 2020. QuantConnect re-creation (SPY/IWM/IYR, 2015-01-01 to 2020-08-16, no fee model described): Sharpe -0.628 versus benchmark 0.582; positive only in the Feb-Mar 2020 crash (1.452). QuantRocket notes most profit came during the financial crisis and that VIX<20 periods lose money (figures only).
entries.risks: R^2 of about 1-2% means a small edge per trade against costs. The 2015-2020 replication suggests the edge decays or is regime-dependent and concentrated in crises. r1 must use the official 16:00 close (the overnight gap is part of the signal). Paper costs exclude commissions. An options version (0DTE for 30 minutes) adds spread and theta that the paper does not cover.
entries.reusable: Signal definitions (prior close to 10:00; 15:00 to 15:30); conditioning on realized vol and volume; out-of-sample R^2 with Clark-West test as the evaluation protocol.
entries.fit: Excellent for the signal: SPY/QQQ 1m bars, one decision a day. The options version is unproven because option P&L can only be recorded going forward.
entries.rank_why: Peer-reviewed, tested out of sample, replicated internationally and in futures, and trivial to reproduce on our data. The A is for the evidence base; recent-period weakness means no edge is assumed.
entries.next: On archived Schwab 1m SPY/QQQ: compute r1 and r12, regress r13 by calendar year, and report hit rate, mean bps per trade, Newey-West t and expanding-window out-of-sample R^2. Split by realized-vol tercile and by |r1| quintile. Cost hurdle: 1-cent spread plus slippage on the ETF. In parallel, record 0DTE ATM option mid and spread at 15:30 and 16:00 to measure option round-trip cost before any options variant.

entries.name: Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum (Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens 2021)
entries.source_version: Journal of Financial Economics 142(1):377-403 (2021); abstract and IDEAS record only (full text paywalled; author PDF link not reachable from this session)
entries.what: Documents market intraday momentum in 60+ equity, bond, commodity and currency futures from 1974 to 2020. The return from the prior close to the last 30 minutes predicts the last-30-minute return, and the paper links this to short-gamma hedging by options market makers and leveraged-ETF rebalancing. The effect reverses over the following days.
entries.entry: Trade in the direction of the return from the prior close to 30 minutes before the close.
entries.exit: Close; no overnight hold (the effect reverses in the following days).
entries.data: Intraday futures data (vendor unknown) and options gamma data (paid). We can only build a gamma proxy going forward from live Schwab chains.
entries.reported: Abstract (paraphrased via IDEAS): 'strong market intraday momentum everywhere'; the predictability is statistically and economically significant and reverses over the following days; linked to hedging demand from options market makers and leveraged ETFs. Specific numbers: unknown (full text not read).
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed JFE. Only the abstract was inspected, so no figures are verified here. Consistent with Gao et al. (2018) and with the Barbon et al. end-of-day paper.
entries.risks: Signing dealer gamma requires an assumption about which side dealers hold, and gamma estimates from open interest are model-dependent. Because of the next-day reversal, positions must be closed at 16:00.
entries.reusable: Dealer net gamma as a regime switch for late-day SPY/QQQ trades (negative gamma means momentum, positive means reversal); a broad cross-asset robustness benchmark.
entries.fit: The signal fits our bars. The gamma filter can only be built going forward, from daily live-chain snapshots.
entries.rank_why: Strong peer-reviewed evidence for the mechanism over a long, cross-asset sample. Its numbers are unverified here because only the abstract was read.
entries.next: Snapshot SPY/QQQ live chains at 15:25 ET daily (OI, IV, strikes) and compute two naive dealer-gamma proxies under opposite dealer-side conventions. After at least 60 sessions, test whether the 15:30-16:00 hit rate of the Gao-style signal differs by gamma sign. Until then, test the unconditional signal on bars.

entries.name: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy for the U.S. Equity Market: 5-min ORB on Stocks in Play (Zarattini, Barbon, Aziz 2024)
entries.source_version: SFI Research Paper 24-98, dated 2024-02-16; full PDF from HSG Alexandria
entries.what: 5-minute opening-range breakout traded only on the day's top 20 'Stocks in Play', ranked by opening-range relative volume, across about 7,000 US stocks from 2016 to 2023.
entries.entry: Filters: open > $5, 14-day average volume >= 1M shares, 14-day ATR > $0.50. RV = first-5-minute volume / 14-day average first-5-minute volume; require RV >= 100% and take the top 20 by RV. A bullish first 5-minute candle allows longs only, a bearish one shorts only, a doji gives no trade. Stop-entry order at the 5-minute high (long) or low (short).
entries.exit: Stop loss at 10% of the 14-day ATR from entry; otherwise exit at 16:00.
entries.sizing: Risk 1% of the capital allocated to that position at the stop; leverage capped at 4x.
entries.data: CRSP plus IQFeed unadjusted intraday data, survivorship-bias-free (paid). For us: Schwab 1m bars; a survivorship-free universe history is the hard part.
entries.reported: Top-20 Stocks-in-Play 5m ORB: total 1,637% net, IRR 41.6%, volatility 14.8%, Sharpe 2.81, hit 48.4%, max drawdown 12%, worst day -1.61%, alpha 35.8%. Base ORB without the RV filter: 29%, Sharpe 0.48. With the RV filter at other windows: 15m 272% (Sharpe 1.43), 30m 21% (Sharpe 0.21), 60m 39% (Sharpe 0.40). Equal-weight combo: 234% (Sharpe 1.99). Commission $0.0035/share; slippage not modeled.
entries.evidence: Author-only; no out-of-sample test (parameters justified by 'economic rationale'). QuantConnect re-implementation (1,000 most liquid stocks, 2016 only): Sharpe 2.396 versus SPY 0.836. QC forum, no numbers: a Python port was 'way worse' in 2023-2025; 'collapses' in 2000-2002; slippage at the open has 'quite a savage effect'; unfilled stop orders filled after hours and inflated returns; live paper trading picked about half the same symbols. Concretum's own data-quality note says the same ORB backtest differed by more than 3x across data vendors (phantom highs/lows, stale bars, early-close leakage, bar assignment).
entries.risks: No slippage on stop entries at the open, in exactly the names whose spreads are widest then. The 5m-versus-15/30/60m gap is unexplained, so the window choice may be data-mined. Top-20 concentration. Results depend on the vendor's OHLC (a phantom high triggers a phantom entry). Short borrow and locates are ignored. In minute backtests the stop is placed a bar after entry. RV is computable at 9:35 (no look-ahead) but ATR and volume filters must use prior-day data.
entries.reusable: The opening-range relative-volume ranking as a catalyst and 'in play' proxy, which is the most practical free substitute for a news feed; ATR-fraction stop; risk-based sizing; first-candle direction filter.
entries.fit: Good for stock signals on 1m bars. Poor for options: single-stock option spreads at 9:35 are wide relative to a 10%-of-ATR stop.
entries.rank_why: Fully specified, and the RV filter is a strong conditions filter, but the evidence is author-only with no slippage, and third parties report execution artifacts and decay.
entries.next: From archived Schwab 1m bars on a liquid universe (with daily universe membership recorded from now on to avoid survivorship), compute the 9:35 RV ranking. Simulate the stop entry with fill = max(stop, next open) plus spread proxy (e.g., 5 bps for names over $20, 15 bps for $5-20) and a 10%-ATR stop. Report net R per trade by year, RV decile and price bucket. Compare 1m, 5m and 15m opening ranges to test the window-sensitivity claim. Record live option spreads at 9:35 for the top-20 names to judge whether any options version can work.

entries.name: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? 5-min ORB on QQQ/TQQQ (Zarattini, Aziz 2023)
entries.source_version: SSRN 4416622 (posted 2023-04-24, revised 2025-09-22): abstract page; rules from Concretum's Python/Alpaca tutorial page; independent replication from an MQL5 blog post
entries.what: The simplest index ORB: the direction of the first 5-minute candle on QQQ sets the side for the day, with a stop at the opposite end of the range. TQQQ is used for leverage.
entries.entry: If the 5th 1m bar closes above the 1st bar's open, go long, otherwise short; enter at the open of the 6th minute (market order, no confirmation).
entries.exit: Stop at the opening-range low (long) or high (short); the tutorial lists a 10R target in H/L mode (the article contradicts itself); otherwise exit at the close. A gap through the stop fills at the bar open.
entries.sizing: shares = min(AUM x 1% / (entry x stop%), 4 x AUM / entry)
entries.instruments: QQQ, TQQQ (the method applies to SPY)
entries.data: Paper vendor unknown; tutorial uses Alpaca free SIP 1m bars, 2016-01-01 to 2026-04-20. Our Schwab bars suffice.
entries.reported: Annualized alpha of 33% over buy-and-hold QQQ, net of commissions; the TQQQ portfolio returned 1,484% versus 169% for QQQ (2016-2023). Per the replication post, the paper's per-trade figures are +0.13R with a 24% hit rate. Tutorial commission $0.0005/share/side, no slippage.
entries.evidence: Independent replication (T. Krueger, MQL5 blog; NQ, SPX, Dow, DAX and FTSE CFDs, Jan 2015 to Jun 2026, about 2,900 sessions each, rules unchanged). Gross NQ +0.131R with 23.2% hits, matching the paper. Net of spread and slippage: NQ +0.002R (t 0.0), SPX -0.081R, Dow -0.081R, DAX -0.038R, FTSE -0.079R. Against a random-direction benchmark the rule still wins by +0.10 to +0.13R in NQ, DAX and FTSE (|t| >= 2). CFD costs were 6-12% of R; ETF costs would be a much smaller fraction, but that is untested.
entries.risks: Edge of about 0.1R per trade, so results are cost-sensitive. A hit rate near 24% means long losing streaks. No confirmation filter, so it trades every non-doji day, including choppy ones. Commission is the only friction modeled.
entries.reusable: Baseline ORB with R accounting; the random-direction benchmark from the replication as a test of the signal itself; the gap-through stop rule.
entries.fit: Excellent for SPY/QQQ underlying tests on 1m bars. An options version must clear the option spread, which is likely larger than the edge for short-dated contracts.
entries.rank_why: The gross effect is independently reproduced, but the net edge on CFDs is zero. On ETFs it is untested and the per-trade edge is small.
entries.next: On Schwab 1m SPY and QQQ: run the exact rule; report gross and net R per trade (1-cent spread plus 1-cent slippage per side) and a 1,000-shuffle random-direction benchmark for a direction t-stat. Use it as the control arm for the confirmation and retest variants (see orb-quantower). Compute the option round-trip cost, from live-recorded chains, that would erase 0.1R.

entries.name: QuantConnect: Opening Range Breakout for Stocks in Play (research post + forum)
entries.source_version: web page and forum pages read 2026-10-31; C# snippets in the post, Python port in comments (not cloned)
entries.what: LEAN re-implementation of the Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz ORB on the 1,000 most liquid US equities, with a community Python port and a long thread of bug reports.
entries.entry: 1,000 most liquid stocks over $5 with 14-day ATR over $0.50; the 20 highest opening-range relative volumes; at 9:35, a stop-market order at the opening bar's high (bullish bar) or low (bearish bar).
entries.exit: Stop at an ATR multiple (value not shown in the text) or at the close.
entries.sizing: 1% of the per-asset allocation at risk, capped at an equal-weight share
entries.data: QuantConnect cloud data (free for cloud backtests under QC terms)
entries.reported: 2016: Sharpe 2.396, beta -0.042, versus SPY buy-and-hold Sharpe 0.836. 17 of 25 parameter combinations beat the benchmark Sharpe; ATR thresholds from $0 to $2 gave Sharpe 1.5-2.7; a percent-of-price ATR filter gave Sharpe 2.237 and PSR 97%.
entries.evidence: Only one year (2016, inside the paper's own sample) is reported, with no costs or slippage stated. Forum reports: Python ATR about 3x too low (indicator warm-up with minute bars); identical results for universes of 20 and 1,000 (suspected bug); unfilled stop orders filled after hours; IBKR paper stop orders landed 20-40 s after entry; slippage modeling 'has quite a savage effect'; live selection differed from the backtest; the 2023-2025 Python port had a worse Sharpe.
entries.risks: As in the paper, plus LEAN minute backtests attach the stop one bar after the entry fill, and the same-bar stop risk is not simulated.
entries.reusable: A ready-made checklist of failure modes to turn into unit tests: warm-up, after-hours fill guard, stop latency, live/backtest universe parity.
entries.fit: Docs only; the logic ports to Python.
entries.rank_why: A useful independent partial replication and bug catalogue, but one in-sample year and no costs.
entries.next: Write the forum's failure modes as assertions in our ORB-SIP simulator: no fills outside 09:30-16:00, ATR from daily bars only, 14-session RV warm-up, stop active from the bar after entry, the same universe for live and backtest. Compare our 2016 Sharpe with 2.396 only if our archive reaches 2016.

entries.name: day-trader-skill
entries.what: 11 Claude skills: scanner (ORB/flags/oversold on Yahoo bars), news (Yahoo RSS + SEC 8-K), entry timer (first 5m close above the 15m OR), exit planner (OR-mid / OR-low / pct / ATR stops, R targets), Time Machine (time-of-day i.i.d. bootstrap of 5m bar ratios, 10,000 replays, + the rule re-run on past sessions), risk/budget/broker (stocks, Alpaca paper), alerts, analyst (XBRL), Pelosi PTRs.
entries.entry: Entry timer: first 5-minute close above the 15-minute opening range (a confirmation close, no retest).
entries.exit: Exit planner: OR-midpoint, OR-low, percent or ATR stops with R-multiple targets.
entries.sizing: Share-based risk/budget module (stocks); options disabled by default.
entries.data: Yahoo bars and Yahoo RSS (free, unofficial), SEC EDGAR 8-K (free), Alpaca paper for the broker module
entries.reported: One worked example (TSLA 2026-10-19 ORB): replays 29.4% target / 25.5% stop / 45.1% neither; history 33 fires: 13 targets, 15 stops, 5 neither, average R -0.062, described as 'close to a coin flip'.
entries.evidence: one worked example (TSLA 2026-10-19 ORB): replays 29.4% target / 25.5% stop / 45.1% neither; history 33 fires 13 T / 15 S / 5 neither, avg R -0.062 -> 'close to a coin flip'. No multi-symbol study, no costs, no out-of-sample.
entries.risks: The Time Machine bootstrap draws each 5m bar ratio independently, ignoring volatility clustering and intraday autocorrelation, which matter for breakout reach odds. Yahoo data is unofficial. A single example, with no costs and no out-of-sample test.
entries.reusable: reach-odds bootstrap idea, rebuilt on Schwab archive bars with today's-volatility scaling and block draws, research-only and calibrated against outcomes; unambiguous ticker-mention regex for source content checks; extra material 8-K items; OR-midpoint stop as an ORBX exit variant; Yahoo per-ticker headline RSS as a discovery lead only
entries.fit: Good conceptually (Python stdlib, EDGAR); stock-only; the bar source must be swapped for the Schwab archive.
entries.rank_why: sound, honest method and clean code, but a single example and stock-only; the bootstrap ignores volatility clustering and intraday autocorrelation (each bar drawn independently), and Yahoo data is unofficial.
entries.next: Rebuild the reach-odds replay on Schwab archive bars with block bootstrap and volatility scaling to today's level. Calibrate predicted target/stop odds against realized outcomes over at least 200 ORB fires, using a Brier score and reliability curve. Test the OR-midpoint stop as an ORB exit variant.

adopted: reach-odds bootstrap idea, rebuilt on Schwab archive bars with today's-volatility scaling and block draws, research-only and calibrated against outcomes
unambiguous ticker-mention regex for source content checks
OR-midpoint stop as an ORBX exit variant
Yahoo per-ticker headline RSS as a discovery lead only

entries.name: QuantRocket first-last (Gao et al. replication in Moonshot)
entries.what: A 20-line Moonshot implementation of first-half-hour / penultimate-half-hour momentum on SPY, with an optional VIX filter.
entries.entry: At 15:30, long if (P_open(10:00) / prior 15:59 close - 1) > 0 and (P_open(15:30) / P_open(15:00) - 1) > 0; short if both are below 0; flat otherwise. Optional MIN_VIX (the notebook uses 20), with VIX read from the 14:00 CT 30-minute bar close (= 15:30 ET).
entries.exit: Close of the 15:59 bar
entries.data: QuantRocket usstock-1min (paid subscription) and Interactive Brokers 30-minute VIX
entries.reported: No numbers in the repo; the notebooks hold tear-sheet figures only. Text: 'Most of the strategy's profitability came during the financial crisis'; 'When the VIX is under 20, the strategy loses money.'
entries.evidence: No numeric results in the repo. Code read in full.
entries.risks: The VIX threshold of 20 was picked after splitting the same backtest's returns by VIX (in-sample selection). Entry is at the 15:30 open, the same price used in the signal (zero latency). Frictions: commission $0.005/share and slippage 0.5 bps only. The source paper is cited as the 2015 SSRN version.
entries.reusable: A short, correct reference for timing conventions (Chicago-time VIX bars, prior-close handling).
entries.fit: The logic ports directly to our bar store; the platform itself is paid, so only the logic is reusable.
entries.rank_why: Faithful and readable, but it reports no numbers and its filter was chosen in-sample.
entries.next: Port the logic. Run with and without a volatility filter, with the threshold picked on the first half of our sample and frozen for the second half. Enter at the 15:31 open instead of the 15:30 signal price.

entries.name: Pervasive Underreaction: Evidence from High-Frequency Data (Jiang, Li, Wang 2021)
entries.source_version: JFE 141(2):573-599 (2021); SSRN abstract plus the Feb 2018 draft 'News Momentum' (full text, Villanova-hosted PDF). Numbers below come from the 2018 draft and may differ in print.
entries.what: Splits stock returns into news-driven parts (15-minute intervals containing RavenPack-tagged news, with overnight news matched to the overnight return) and no-news parts. News-driven returns keep drifting for days without reversal; no-news returns reverse.
entries.entry: Buy the top news-return decile and sell the bottom decile (cross-sectional, weekly in the draft).
entries.exit: About one week in the strategy; in event time the drift keeps accumulating for longer.
entries.instruments: US common stocks (5,480 firms in the draft)
entries.data: RavenPack (paid; relevance and novelty score filters) plus TAQ (paid), Mar 2000 to Oct 2012
entries.reported: 2018 draft: news decile spread 3.34%/month (t = 11.72), FFC4 alpha 3.37%/month. Equal-weighted strategy 40.08% annualized gross, Sharpe about 3.29, max drawdown 15.92%, but a daily cost of 21.7 bps exceeds its 15.9 bps return, so it is not profitable net. Value-weighted: 8.3 bps cost against 11.7 bps return, about 8.6%/yr net. Overnight news spread: 17 bps at the 16:00 close, 59 bps at the next open, 104 bps by t+4. Strongest in small, low-coverage and illiquid stocks.
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed (JFE). I read the 2018 draft rather than the published version.
entries.risks: Net profits are thin and concentrated in value-weighted (large) names. RavenPack's novelty and relevance filtering can't be reproduced with free news. EDGAR timestamps lag the newswires. The documented drift is multi-day, while our desk is intraday.
entries.reusable: The news versus no-news decomposition as a classifier: continuation after news-driven moves, reversal after no-news moves. Matching news timestamps to intraday intervals.
entries.fit: Partial: needs trustworthy timestamps; the intraday continuation part is testable with EDGAR acceptance times.
entries.rank_why: Credible evidence that news moves continue, but the result is cost-sensitive, multi-day, and built on paid news we can't reproduce.
entries.next: Build an event table from EDGAR 8-K acceptance timestamps (plus free press-release timestamps you trust) for 2-3 years. For events between 9:45 and 15:00, measure 1m returns from t+5 to t+30, t+60 and t+120 minutes, conditional on the sign of the first 5-minute reaction and on relative volume. Compare against matched large no-news moves, which should reverse if the paper holds.

entries.name: Rest in Peace Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (Martineau 2022)
entries.source_version: Critical Finance Review 11(3-4):613-646 (Aug 2022); abstract via IDEAS (the CFR PDF host is not reachable from this session)
entries.what: Argues that modern prices fully reflect earnings surprises on the announcement date, so multi-day PEAD has disappeared: since 2006 for large stocks, and only recently for microcaps.
entries.entry: n/a (negative result)
entries.exit: n/a
entries.timeframe: Announcement day and the following days
entries.data: unknown (abstract only; presumably CRSP/Compustat/IBES, all paid)
entries.reported: Abstract (paraphrased): PEAD absent for large stocks since 2006, recently vanished for microcaps; stock prices fully reflect earnings surprises on the announcement date.
entries.evidence: Published in CFR; only the abstract was read. Consistent with Busse and Green (2002) on speed. A contrary lead ('Is post-earnings announcement drift a thing again?', UCLA Anderson Review) was found but not read.
entries.risks: Says nothing about intraday dynamics on day 0 itself. If correct, multi-day earnings-continuation holds in large caps have no edge.
entries.reusable: Design rule: earnings and catalyst continuation must be tested as day-0 intraday trades, not multi-day drift.
entries.fit: Directly decision-relevant for the news priority; testable with EDGAR Item 2.02 timestamps.
entries.rank_why: A credible, published negative result that is directly decision-relevant and checkable on our data.
entries.next: Tag 8-K Item 2.02 filings. For large caps, measure open-to-close and close-to-day-5 returns conditional on gap sign and opening-range RV. Expect multi-day drift near zero, and test whether 9:45-16:00 continuation after gaps with RV > 2 exists.

entries.name: Market Efficiency in Real Time (Busse, Green 2002)
entries.source_version: JFE 65(3):415-437 (Sept 2002); full text paywalled. Findings taken from an Alpha Architect summary. Related: Rogers, Skinner, Zechman (2017), 'Run EDGAR Run', JAR 55(2):459-505 (university summary read).
entries.what: Event study of CNBC Morning and Midday Call stock reports: prices react within seconds, and positive reports are fully priced within about a minute.
entries.entry: Their profitability test trades within 15 seconds of the first mention, in the report's direction.
entries.exit: Short horizon (exact rule unknown)
entries.data: TAQ plus CNBC broadcast timestamps, Jun 12 to Oct 27 2000: 322 reports over 84 trading days (per summary)
entries.reported: Per summary: prices respond 'within seconds of initial mention'; positive reports are 'fully incorporated within one minute'; trading intensity roughly doubles in the first minute; trades within 15 seconds earned small but significant profits (blogger's estimate: about 40 bp gross, 20-30 bp net); negative news shows some drift. Rogers et al.: in 2012-2013 just over half of filings reached paying PDS subscribers before EDGAR web posting, on average 18 seconds earlier.
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed but old (2000 sample, 322 events), and the full text was not read.
entries.risks: Implies that a human placing orders by hand cannot capture the first-minute reaction. Any edge for DeltaDesk must come from continuation over the following minutes to hours. EDGAR-based alerts may start late.
entries.reusable: A latency budget: start every news-strategy clock at our ingestion time plus human order time, never at the filing timestamp.
entries.fit: A constraint rather than a strategy; directly relevant to the EDGAR and news inputs.
entries.rank_why: Credible but old and not read in full; it describes a speed race we can't win and is useful mainly as a design constraint.
entries.next: For every 8-K we ingest, log EDGAR acceptance time, our receipt time and the 1m path. Estimate the share of the 0-30 minute move completed before receipt + 60 s (human latency) and drop event types where most of the move is already gone.

entries.name: The Role of Leveraged ETFs and Option Market Imbalances on End-of-Day Price Dynamics (Barbon, Beckmeyer, Buraschi, Moerke 2021)
entries.source_version: S/BF-HSG Working Paper on Finance 2021/14 (Sept 2021), previously titled 'End-of-Day Momentum and Option Hedging'; institutional PDF read through the fetch tool (extract may be partial). Publication status unknown.
entries.what: Single-stock end-of-day momentum or reversal driven by dealer gamma imbalance and by leveraged-ETF rebalancing; most of the gamma effect reverses at the next open.
entries.entry: At 15:30, sort on Gamma_HP = 100 x gamma imbalance (scaled by last-30-minute dollar volume) x r_pre (prior close to 15:30). Negative Gamma_HP (dealers must buy into strength) means continuation.
entries.exit: Close; about 82% of the gamma effect reverses at the next open (about 32% for LETF).
entries.instruments: Optionable US stocks held in leveraged ETFs (72 LETFs on 24 benchmarks)
entries.data: Signed option volume by participant type from 5 exchanges (CBOE C1, GEMX, ISE, PHLX, BX) plus OptionMetrics (paid), May 2005 to Jul 2020; LETF data 2012-2019
entries.reported: Gamma_HP coefficient on end-of-day returns -11.95 (t = -5.37). 2012-2019 equal-weighted: eta(Gamma_HP) 5.16%/yr, Sharpe 4.13, success 62.34%; eta(LETF) 11.82%/yr, Sharpe 4.65; combined 11.00%/yr, Sharpe 5.09. Value-weighted combined: 6.21%/yr, Sharpe 3.14.
entries.evidence: Working paper; read via an extract of the institutional PDF. Transaction costs not stated in the parts read.
entries.risks: Needs a signed customer/dealer open-interest history (paid). Trading single stocks in the last 30 minutes at 5-11%/yr gross is cost-fragile, and a decile Sharpe above 4 before costs signals strong cost sensitivity. Dealer-side assumptions drive the gamma sign.
entries.reusable: LETF rebalancing demand (computable from public issuer AUM and leverage) and dollar-volume-scaled gamma as late-day regime variables for SPY/QQQ.
entries.fit: Partial. LETF demand for SPY/QQQ is computable for free; dealer gamma only going forward from live chains.
entries.rank_why: Credible mechanism over a large sample, but it relies on paid signed-volume data, costs are unknown, and the trades are single-stock last-30-minute ones.
entries.next: Estimate daily LETF rebalancing demand for SPY/QQQ, the sum of AUM x L x (L - 1) x r_pre over the 2x/3x/inverse funds from issuer-published AUM, and test whether it predicts the sign and size of the 15:30-16:00 return on our 1m bars, alone and combined with the Gao r1 signal.

entries.name: When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses? (Kaminski, Lo 2014)
entries.source_version: Journal of Financial Markets 18:234-254 (2014); abstract via IDEAS (MIT DSpace PDF exists but was not read in full)
entries.what: An analytical framework (the 'stopping premium') for when stop-loss rules add or subtract value, given the return process; tested on index futures with daily data.
entries.entry: n/a
entries.exit: Exit after cumulative losses cross a threshold and re-enter later; value depends on serial correlation and regime structure.
entries.instruments: Index futures (daily) in the empirical part
entries.data: Daily futures prices
entries.reported: Abstract (paraphrased): at longer sampling frequencies some stop-loss policies 'can increase expected return' while substantially reducing volatility.
entries.evidence: Peer-reviewed; daily data, not intraday. Abstract-level read.
entries.risks: The conclusions don't transfer to 1m intraday exits automatically; our own intraday autocorrelation has to be measured.
entries.reusable: A way to evaluate trailing and momentum-failure exits: compare E[R] and variance with and without the stop given measured autocorrelation, instead of picking exits off equity curves.
entries.fit: Medium: a method, not a ready intraday rule.
entries.rank_why: Credible theory and evidence, but only indirectly applicable to intraday trailing exits.
entries.next: For BTM and ORB entries on SPY/QQQ, measure post-entry 1m/5m return autocorrelation. Compare exits on identical entries: EOD only; VWAP/band trail (BTM); ATR-chandelier (3 x 1m-ATR(14) from the high); MACD(13,21) fade (Alpaca example); OR-midpoint stop. Use paired per-trade differences, and accept an exit only if it improves net R in both halves of the sample.

entries.name: backtesting.py
entries.what: Python event-driven single-instrument bar backtester with stop/limit orders, SL/TP brackets, a constant relative spread, and commissions.
entries.entry: Framework. Market orders fill at the next bar's open by default (trade_on_close=False); stop orders fill at max(open, stop) for buys and min(open, stop) for sells, so gaps through the stop are handled.
entries.exit: SL/TP contingent orders. SL orders are queued first, so if SL and TP both hit in one bar, SL wins (pessimistic). If a new trade's SL/TP would execute inside its own entry bar, it issues a warning and defers to the next bar (issue #119).
entries.sizing: Fraction of equity or units; margin/leverage parameter
entries.data: User-supplied OHLCV (free)
entries.reported: n/a (framework)
entries.evidence: Code read at this SHA (Broker._process_orders, Order/Trade contingent logic). Ships a test suite (backtesting/test). No strategy claims.
entries.risks: Single asset only, so no cross-sectional stocks-in-play portfolio. The spread is a constant fraction (no time-of-day widening at the open). The entry-bar SL deferral can understate losses on volatile 1m bars (it warns). AGPL means not vendoring it into anything distributed.
entries.reusable: Its fill rules as the reference spec for our own simulator; parameter heatmaps for stability checks.
entries.fit: Good for SPY/QQQ single-underlying 1m tests in Python; no options or multi-asset support.
entries.rank_why: Conservative, documented intrabar semantics, readable code, Python, free, and a match for our first tests.
entries.next: Implement BTM and the QQQ ORB in backtesting.py on Schwab 1m bars as an independent check on our in-house simulator; any P&L difference over 5% on identical trades must be explained trade by trade.

entries.name: PyBroker
entries.what: Python multi-symbol backtester with walk-forward analysis, bootstrapped metrics and pluggable slippage models.
entries.entry: Framework. buy_delay and sell_delay default to 1 bar, so signals never fill on their own bar by default.
entries.exit: Price stops are evaluated in fixed order: loss, then profit, then trailing; the first to trigger exits (conservative). Bar-count stops are evaluated after price stops. Stops are not evaluated on the entry bar, and missing or halted bars do not trigger stops on stale OHLC.
entries.sizing: Framework (shares, percent of equity; position caps)
entries.data: User-supplied or built-in sources (free options exist)
entries.reported: n/a
entries.evidence: Code read at this SHA (config.py, portfolio.check_stops, slippage.py, the walk-forward mixin). Slippage models: Fixed, Volatility and Volume; slippage only ever worsens fills. bootstrap_samples defaults to 10,000.
entries.risks: The intrabar path is not modeled beyond loss-first precedence. No options support. The Commons Clause forbids selling it (fine for personal use). Not verified on 1m intraday sessions with half-days.
entries.reusable: Walk-forward windows plus bootstrap confidence intervals for Sharpe and profit factor, and the volume slippage model, for the cross-sectional ORB-SIP test.
entries.fit: Good for multi-stock intraday research in Python.
entries.rank_why: Sound defaults and evaluation tooling, but not yet verified on our 1m data and it doesn't model the intrabar path.
entries.next: Hand-build a 3-session 1m fixture that includes a gap through a stop, SL and TP in the same bar, and an early close. Confirm the expected fills, then use PyBroker's walk-forward and bootstrap for the ORB-SIP universe test.

entries.name: vectorbt (open-source)
entries.what: Numba-vectorized portfolio simulation for fast parameter sweeps (from_signals/from_orders) with SL, TP and trailing stops.
entries.entry: Framework. The default order price is np.inf, which means the current close, so a signal computed on a bar's close fills at that same close unless the user shifts it.
entries.exit: SL is checked before TP within a bar (pessimistic). A stop gapped past the open fills at the open. The trailing stop is updated with the bar high/low after the stop check, so there is no same-bar look-ahead. A stop can't trigger on the entry bar ('only one signal per asset and bar'). StopExitPrice options: StopLimit, StopMarket, Price, Close.
entries.data: User-supplied
entries.reported: n/a
entries.evidence: Code read at this SHA (vectorbt/portfolio/nb.py get_stop_price_nb and the from_signals loop; enums.py).
entries.risks: Default close fills invite look-ahead. Entry-bar stop risk is ignored. The Commons Clause applies. The paid PRO edition is not needed and was not used.
entries.reusable: Robustness surfaces such as BTM band multiplier x lookback, or ORB window x stop fraction, once prices are shifted to next open and fees and slippage are set.
entries.fit: Good for sweeps; not the source of record for P&L.
entries.rank_why: Fast and its stop semantics are sound, but its defaults make it easy to fool yourself.
entries.next: Use only for sensitivity grids with price = next open and nonzero fees and slippage; every reported vectorbt result must be reproduced trade-for-trade in backtesting.py or our simulator.

entries.name: NautilusTrader
entries.what: Rust/Python event-driven engine with a matching engine, fill models, latency models and option instruments; sparse checkout of execution models and backtesting docs only.
entries.entry: Framework. Bars must be timestamped at the interval close (ts_init) so a bar isn't visible before it forms. With bar_execution, each bar becomes 4 synthetic L1 updates. The default path is Open-High-Low-Close; optional adaptive ordering visits the extreme nearest the open first, which the docs call a 'deterministic heuristic'.
entries.exit: Resting stops and limits match against the synthetic path. Orders submitted in on_bar settle against the bar-close book unless a LatencyModel delays them.
entries.data: User-supplied or adapters
entries.reported: n/a
entries.evidence: Docs read at this SHA (docs/concepts/backtesting/bar-execution.md, fill-models.md, data-and-venues.md); file list of crates/execution/src/models (fee.rs, fill.rs, latency.rs). DefaultFillModel: prob_fill_on_limit = 1.0, prob_slippage = 0.0. The docs warn that bars can't establish intrabar order, spread, depth or queue position. version.json reads v2.0.0rc9.
entries.risks: The default O-H-L-C path is optimistic for a long with the target above and the stop below, since the high is visited first; it needs adaptive ordering or a pessimistic override. Zero slippage by default. Heavy toolchain, and the version is a release candidate.
entries.reusable: Latency-model and probabilistic-slippage concepts; the close-timestamp convention for bars; option instruments for replaying recorded live chains later.
entries.fit: Too heavy for now; the best open-source candidate for quote-level replay of options once we've recorded live chains.
entries.rank_why: The most realistic execution modeling found, but its defaults are optimistic for bars and the complexity is high for a personal desk.
entries.next: After at least 3 months of recorded live SPY option quotes, prototype one BTM options variant with a 1-2 s latency model and slippage calibrated to the recorded spreads, and compare it with the bar-only simulator.

entries.name: QuantConnect LEAN (fill and slippage models)
entries.what: C# algorithmic trading engine behind QuantConnect; only Common/Orders/Fills and Common/Orders/Slippage were checked out and read.
entries.entry: Framework. EquityFillModel.StopMarketFill uses the trade bar that closes after the order time; a gap through the stop fills at the bar open minus/plus slippage. Market orders fill at the best-effort ask/bid (quotes) plus slippage, and wait for fresh data when prices are stale.
entries.exit: Same fill models
entries.data: QuantConnect/LEAN data formats
entries.reported: n/a
entries.evidence: Code read at this SHA. Slippage models present: Constant, VolumeShare (price impact x (order/volume)^2), MarketImpact, Null, AlphaStreams. The default slippage depends on the brokerage model (not verified).
entries.risks: C# core, and Python via pythonnet is heavy. With trade bars only, fills use trade prices (no spread). Minute-resolution stops attach a bar after entry (per the QC forum).
entries.reusable: The VolumeShare and MarketImpact slippage formulas for opening stop entries in stocks-in-play; the gap-through stop rule.
entries.fit: Poor as our runtime; good as a reference for fill models.
entries.rank_why: Realistic, well-used fill logic worth copying, but not a fit as the desk's engine.
entries.next: Port the VolumeShareSlippageModel formula into our simulator and rerun the ORB-SIP test with it; report how much net R drops relative to fixed-bps slippage.

entries.name: orb-quantower (confirmation close + retest-limit ORB)
entries.what: C#/.NET 8 Quantower indicator and strategy for futures: first breakout of the opening range, confirmed by a bar close beyond an extension, with an optional limit entry back at the range boundary (retest).
entries.entry: The opening range is built from bar highs and lows in [start, start + duration), default 15 minutes from 13:30 UTC. On each closed bar (default 1m), if close > OR high + 10% of range, go long; if close < OR low - 10%, go short. Entry is either Market (next bar) or Limit at the OR boundary (fills only on a pullback, i.e. a retest). One trade per UTC session.
entries.exit: Bracket: stop at the opposite extension line, target = entry +/- R:R (default 2.0) x risk.
entries.sizing: Contracts = balance x risk% / (stop distance in ticks x tick value), capped by MaxContracts
entries.data: Broker or Market Replay feed via Quantower
entries.reported: None; the README tells users to test it themselves.
entries.evidence: No performance evidence. xUnit tests for the range engine, decider and risk calculator (33 [Fact]/[Theory] markers counted). Code read at this SHA. Uses the closed bar ([1] from end), so no look-ahead in the decision.
entries.risks: LastEntryTime is computed and logged in OnRun but never passed to BreakoutDecider, so the documented entry cutoff is not enforced at this commit. Resting retest limit orders have no expiry or cancel logic. Sessions and windows are fixed UTC, so the US open shifts an hour across DST unless reconfigured. Stopping at the opposite extension (about 1.2x the range) makes R targets far away.
entries.reusable: The cleanest confirm-then-retest ORB logic found (pure, testable decider): confirmation close beyond an extension, then a limit at the broken level.
entries.fit: Wrong platform and language, but the logic ports to Python in an hour.
entries.rank_why: The only inspected implementation of breakout, confirmation and retest, clean and unit-tested, but with no performance evidence and two logic gaps.
entries.next: Port the decider to Python. On SPY, QQQ and the stocks-in-play universe (1m bars), compare on the same days: (a) stop entry at the OR extreme (the Zarattini control); (b) market entry after a confirmation close beyond the 10% extension; (c) limit at the OR boundary after confirmation, with a 60-minute expiry (retest). Report fill rate, net R, and adverse selection (outcome of retest-filled versus unfilled confirmed days).

entries.name: Opening-Range-Breakout-Strategy-in-Python (umerdawood23)
entries.license: none found (no LICENSE file; the README shows an MIT badge)
entries.what: One notebook adapting Concretum's ORB backtest kernel to Yahoo Finance TQQQ data.
entries.entry: Direction = sign(close of bar orb_m-1 - open of bar 0); market entry at the open of bar orb_m.
entries.exit: Stop at the OR low/high (as % from entry); optional R target (default inf); otherwise the last close. If stop and target first hit on the same bar index, the stop wins. A gap through the stop fills at the bar open.
entries.sizing: min(AUM x 1% / (entry x stop%), 4 x AUM / entry) shares
entries.data: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (free, unofficial)
entries.reported: README example: Total Return 148.72%, CAGR 35.41%, Volatility 42.18%, Sharpe 1.24, Max Drawdown -28.76%. The README text begins 'Here's a comprehensive README.md file for your GitHub repository', so it looks machine-generated and the numbers aren't tied to any run.
entries.evidence: None. Code read in full (16.8k characters of notebook code).
entries.risks: It requests 2016-2023 intraday data that Yahoo does not serve (the README itself says 1m covers only the last 30 days). With 5m bars, orb_m = 5 counts bars, so the range is 25 minutes, not 5. Timestamps are shifted +1 minute regardless of interval. ATR is computed but unused. The README references config.py and strategies.py, which don't exist.
entries.reusable: Nothing beyond Concretum's own tutorial; the stop-first tie rule and gap fill are fine.
entries.fit: Poor
entries.rank_why: Broken data assumptions, a bar-count bug, and fabricated-looking README results.
entries.next: None; use our own implementation of the QQQ ORB entry.

entries.name: opening_range_breakout (westonplatter)
entries.what: 2020 Python/Ruby experiments with ORB on MES futures: bracket orders, tiered targets, a trailing third unit, and re-arming after price returns to the range.
entries.entry: simple.py: OR = max/min of closes between 12:30:00 and 12:30:30 UTC (hard-coded; a comment notes the DST issue). Market entry at the bar close when close >= OR high or <= OR low.
entries.exit: Long stop = max(close - 2 pts, OR mid + 0.5); targets at +4 and +10.5 pts; a third unit uses a 4-pt trailing stop with a +34-pt cap; flatten at 19:45 UTC. Re-entry is allowed after price returns inside OR +/- 1.5 pts.
entries.data: MES CSVs (only mes-july2020.csv is included; simple.py reads a file that isn't in the repo)
entries.reported: None
entries.evidence: None. Code read in full.
entries.risks: orbo.py has a syntax error (assignment inside a list comprehension) and uses order_uuid before it is assigned, so it can't run. simple.py fills stops and limits at the bar close, not the stop price, and declares slippage = 0.25 without applying it. The UTC window breaks with DST. 'pts' P&L sums signed prices.
entries.reusable: The 're-arm only after re-entering OR +/- extension' gate as a crude retest condition; an OR-midpoint stop floor.
entries.fit: Poor
entries.rank_why: Unfinished and partly unrunnable, with close-price fills.
entries.next: None beyond adding the re-arm gate as one variant in the orb-quantower retest comparison.

entries.name: orb-bot (IDEXAONE)
entries.what: Live Alpaca paper bot: long-only 15-minute ORB on SPY, QQQ and IWM, polling every 2 minutes.
entries.entry: Between 9:45 and 11:30 ET, if the latest ask is above the OR high, market-buy a fixed $19,759 notional with a bracket.
entries.exit: Stop at the OR low; target at entry + 2 x OR height; force flat at 15:55.
entries.data: Alpaca (free key)
entries.reported: README 'Verified backtest' 2024-05-01 to 2026-05-01: 1,462 trades, win 44.32%, total +10.99%, Sharpe 1.29, max drawdown -2.54%, profit factor 1.18. 2025-05-01 to 2026-05-01: 734 trades, win 42.78%, +2.78%, Sharpe 0.74, profit factor 1.09.
entries.evidence: No backtest code in the repo, so the claims can't be verified. 1,462 trades in about 2 years at most 3 per day means a long trigger on about 97% of symbol-days, which is implausible for 'above the 15-minute high before 11:30' and suggests the backtest rules differ from the bot.
entries.risks: The signal is an ask-quote snapshot every 2 minutes (stale and spread-inflated), with no confirmation. The README contains unverified regulatory statements and promotes an index site.
entries.reusable: None notable
entries.fit: Poor
entries.rank_why: Unverifiable, internally implausible claims and a crude live loop.
entries.next: None; long-only and 15-minute variants are parameters of the QQQ ORB test.

entries.name: quant-trading: Dual Thrust backtest (je-suis-tm)
entries.what: A widely shared collection of strategy scripts; inspected 'Dual Thrust backtest.py', an open-range breakout variant, on GBPUSD minute data.
entries.entry: At 03:00, upper = price + 0.5 x range and lower = price - 0.5 x range, where range = max(HH - LC, HC - LL) over rg = 5 days. Long above upper, short below lower; reversal allowed.
entries.exit: Flatten at 12:00
entries.data: gbpusd.csv
entries.reported: None (plot only)
entries.evidence: None. Code read in full.
entries.risks: Look-ahead: min2day builds each day's H/L/C from that day's 03:00-12:00 data, and rolling(5) at today's row includes today, which is then used at 03:00 to set today's trigger levels. Today's future range leaks into the triggers. No P&L and no costs; hard-coded os.chdir('D:/').
entries.reusable: The Dual Thrust threshold formula, if shifted one day, as an alternative breakout band to the BTM noise area.
entries.fit: Poor
entries.rank_why: Look-ahead bias, and no P&L.
entries.next: Optional: Dual Thrust with range.shift(1) as a baseline band against the BTM noise area on SPY.

entries.name: Momentum-Trading-Example (alpacahq)
entries.what: 2019 live-only example: low-priced gap-up stocks, buy a break of the 15-minute high with MACD confirmation, structure stop, 3R target with an exit on MACD fade.
entries.entry: Universe: price $2-$13, prior-day dollar volume over $500k, today's change >= 3.5% at scan time. Between 9:45 and 10:30: change from the prior close over 4%, price above the 15-minute high, today's volume over 30k, MACD(12,26) histogram >= 0 and rising for 3 bars, MACD(40,60) >= 0 and rising. Limit buy at the last price, cancelled after more than 1 minute.
entries.exit: Stop = last 5-minute pivot low - $0.01 (fallback: 5% below). Sell at the 3R target only once MACD(13,21) <= 0; also sell below cost basis when MACD <= 0. Liquidate 15 minutes before the close.
entries.data: Polygon through legacy alpaca_trade_api endpoints (not part of the current alpaca-py SDK)
entries.reported: None
entries.evidence: No backtest. Code read in full.
entries.risks: Nothing is tested. The pre-open wait loop never refreshes the current time (an infinite loop if started before 9:44). The old 'ta' API. Sub-$13 stocks bring wide spreads and halts. The 'news' catalyst is only proxied by percent change.
entries.reusable: The pivot-low structure stop; the MACD-fade exit (let winners run past the target until momentum turns); limit-then-cancel entry discipline.
entries.fit: The logic is relevant to momentum confirmation and failure detection; the code isn't usable.
entries.rank_why: Untested live example with stale APIs and a startup bug; only the exit ideas are reusable.
entries.next: Include the pivot-low stop and the MACD(13,21)-fade exit as candidates in the Kaminski-Lo exit comparison.

entries.name: LiuAlgoTrader (momentum_long + backtester)
entries.what: Python async framework (Alpaca/Polygon, PostgreSQL) with a momentum scanner and a 'momentum_long' strategy that evolved from the Alpaca example, plus a backtester.
entries.entry: Close above the 15-minute high; MACD > 0, rising 3 bars, MACD > 1.1 x signal, histogram rising; VWAP > open > prior bar close; RSI(20) < 75, otherwise a 5-minute cooldown. Stop from support/resistance at VWAP; target 3R. Market order in the first 30 minutes, otherwise a limit at max(close, vwap).
entries.exit: Stop on the bar close; MACD(13,21) bearish-cross bail-outs; partial scalp at +4% or above the midpoint to target; whipsaw handling.
entries.data: Alpaca/Polygon keys; PostgreSQL
entries.reported: None in the inspected files
entries.evidence: None. Read scanners/momentum.py, examples/quickstart/momentum_long_simplified.py and enhanced_backtest.py.
entries.risks: calculate_execution_price fills market orders at close[now], the same bar close the strategy just used to decide, so latency is zero. Limit buys fill at that close if it's at or below the limit. Stops are checked on the bar close, not the low, which understates wicks and gaps. Only percentage fees, no slippage. Last commit 2023-01, on the deprecated alpaca_trade_api.
entries.reusable: The scanner/strategy separation and trade-log schema; momentum-failure exit rules as candidates.
entries.fit: Poor (stale dependencies, database, optimistic fills)
entries.rank_why: Its backtester fills at the signal bar's close and checks stops on the close.
entries.next: None; borrow exit-rule ideas only.
